title: Request for an article 64(2) opinion from the IE SA on AI models

covered_actors: data controllers training, developing, or operating AI models using personal data

evidence.quote: The IE SA hereby requests that the EDPB examine the within matters of general application (and which produce effects in more than one Member State) and issue an opinion on the said matters pursuant to Article 64(2) GDPR (the “Request”).

policy_extraction.implementation_notes: This document is a formal procedural request from the Irish Supervisory Authority (IE SA) to the European Data Protection Board (EDPB) seeking an Article 64(2) GDPR opinion on AI models (including large language models). It does not itself impose new binding obligations or issue final guidance; instead, it frames four interpretive questions under the GDPR and Law Enforcement Directive (LED)—explicitly excluding the EU AI Act, DMA, DGA, and DSA—concerning model anonymity, legitimate interests as a legal basis for training and post-training processing, and the downstream effect of unlawfully processed training data.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document is exclusively framed around fundamental rights, specifically personal-data privacy and data protection under the GDPR and Law Enforcement Directive. The Irish Supervisory Authority justifies seeking a harmonised EDPB opinion on the need to address wide-ranging data protection concerns affecting data subjects across the EU/EEA, resolve data subject complaints, mitigate personal data exposure vulnerabilities, and ensure that controllers appropriately balance their interests against the interests of data subjects. No other risk frames such as innovation enablement, economic competitiveness, or public safety are invoked as governance rationales.

evidence_spans.quote: The training and use of AI Models, including so-called “large language models”, gives rise to a number of wide-ranging data protection concerns. The issues arising impact data subjects across the EU/EEA.

The IE SA has received a number of complaints both from data subjects in Ireland and from data subjects throughout the EEA, by way of referrals from other SAs, which raise questions concerning the extent to which the processing of personal data associated with the development of AI Models complies with the GDPR.
